---
title: "How do I visualize the probability below a cutoff under a normal model?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I visualize the probability below a cutoff under a normal model?

## Steps to decide and solve

Establish a modeling reason for treating the variable as normal; state the chosen mean, standard deviation and cutoff; shade the area that corresponds to the inequality.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
mu <- mean(d$Sepal.Length)
sigma <- sd(d$Sepal.Length)
p <- ru_apply("normal_shaded_area", mu=mu, sigma=sigma,
              threshold=6, assume_normal=TRUE)
stopifnot(p>0,p<1)
```

This models sepal length with an illustrative normal approximation fitted to pooled flowers. The assumption is not established: the dataset combines distinct species. The shaded area is a model prediction, not the observed fraction below the cutoff.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("normal_shaded_area", mu=mean(your_data$numeric_column), sigma=sd(your_data$numeric_column), threshold=6, assume_normal=TRUE)
```

If asked for the empirical percentage below the cutoff, calculate mean(d$Sepal.Length < 6) rather than assuming a normal curve.

Use `ru_plan("normal_shaded_area")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
